slot_note: supply-chain-logistics x forecasting; first realisation of analytical_tasks note FC01; pilot batch of seven, registration deferred to the batch step
niche: a city's contracted demand for the new dedicated utility service that will feed two permit-only garage decks once their 6.6 kW Level 2 charging pedestals are replaced by 11.5 kW units, committed for the first contract year under a twelve-month demand ratchet
answer: File 130 kW as the contracted demand for the first contract year, April 2027 to March 2028.
stakeholder_role: the city's energy manager, who buys utility service for city facilities and signs the service agreement

spine.entity: one 15-minute energy reading on one settled charging session at one of the city's eight garages
spine.source: synthetic (fictional city's charging network settlement export, January 2024 to December 2026)

world.org_type: a city's parking services division that runs Level 2 charging in eight municipal garages, with the city energy manager contracting its utility service

driver: The forward peak of a summed load turns on a per-unit draw cap that is an attribute of a different entity reached through a dated join, replayed over closed operations that the export records at a finer grain: the closed record certifies a unit-level replay that takes that attribute as of each closed event, but the population that will carry the forward window was re-registered after the last closed event, and a daily settlement cut splits every operation still running into two records that meet end to start, which the closed draw cannot tell from one operation; replayed record by record the split operations restart at full draw after the cut and overstate the forward peak, and only the records joined back into operations reproduce the per-operation counts a billing file publishes.
driver_concrete: Every 2026 session at the Civic Center decks drew the old pedestals' 6.6 kW; on the new 11.5 kW units each session draws the smaller of 11.5 kW and its car's onboard charger rating, reached through session, permit, vehicle check and the Parking Services reference list, and the car is the one the permit carries in the contract year (at the January 2027 renewal 18 county permits moved from 2020 Bolt EVs at 7.2 kW to 2023 Bolt EVs at 11.0 kW). Curbline's daily settlement run, from 10:00 a.m., closes every session still charging and carries the charge on in a new record from that second at the same unit under the same permit or card; 3,033 of the decks' 2026 charges are such pairs. Replayed record by record with the contract-year cars the billed maximum is 155.4 kW (155 filed, 160 rounded up) at noon on 8 December 2026, and with each record's car on its own date 162.2 kW in February; joined into charges, the only reading whose counts reproduce all 875 permit-months of Parking Services' 2026 charging statements, the contract year's billed maximum is 129.1 kW (130 filed) in the same quarter-hour, against 148.5 kW with the 2026 cars on charges, 103.0 kW for the replay at the rating and 98.6 kW at the Library vans' 11.0 kW.
stump: A competent solver replays every 2026 deck session record on the new units at the smaller of 11.5 kW and the onboard rating of the car its permit carries in the contract year, grows by the filed 1.12 and files 155 kW (155.4 unrounded, 160 rounded up, set at noon on 8 December 2026); the step that lands it there is replaying each settlement record as a charge of its own: Curbline's daily settlement run from 10:00 a.m. closes every session still charging and carries the charge on in a new record from that second, so record by record each charge's second record restarts at the run at the car's full new rate and cars that finish before noon as one charge are back on the meter at noon; joined back into charges (3,033 zero-gap pairs at the decks in 2026, whose counts reproduce every permit-month of Parking Services' charging statements) the contracted demand is 130 kW, set in the same quarter-hour.

differentiation.task37: task37 conditions a forward count on a linked entity still holding its authorisation when the qualifying step ends, an absolute split recovered from a closed roll that cuts a count; here the linked entity is the car behind a permit, the date that matters is the contract year after a dated renewal, and the graded quantity is a coincident 15-minute maximum re-timed by each car's charging limit, which the renewal moves to a different month rather than cutting a total.
differentiation.task44: task44 measures a behavioural moderator over a prior instance of the forward window to split a pilot's pooled effect into opposite-signed item effects and count the gainers; here nothing is re-measured over another window: each forward session draws the smaller of the new rating and a fixed attribute of the car its permit carries after a dated renewal, and the graded quantity is a billed quarter-hour maximum, not a count of items.
differentiation.task97: task97 forecasts renewals from a place's cumulative history across every occupant, carried through a retired system's account conversion; here the history is not cumulated at all: each closed session is replayed with the car its permit will carry in the contract year, a re-registration dated after the last closed session, and the forward quantity is a coincident peak set by which cars still charge into the billed window.

A as decisive is banned against task114, and (time, A) is spent in task107 and nine older builds. Context artifact redrawn from the network operator's monthly peak report (monitoring_export, banned against task116) to the facilities electricians' monthly sub-meter log for the two deck charging panels (operations_log). Forum and forcing event redrawn from the utility (customer_or_counterparty) and its contract deadline (purchase_order_or_contract), both banned against task114, to city council approval of the service agreement and the switchover onto the new dedicated service. Spine rows, deliverables, opening move and answer updated from the cut pack and submission.md at stage 3 (2026-10-09); driver_concrete restated with the as-built figures. Harden loop 1 (2026-10-09), same architecture: round 1's plain solver executed the per-car onboard limit as a work order and landed 150 kW, so a rung was added after it: the car each permit carries in the contract year (the January 2027 renewal), from the measured catalogue's #5 (population as of the governing date) with #13 as the frame; G6 (composition shift) added to the generators; the registry's plate column dropped; answer, stump, driver, driver_concrete and spine rows restated from the rebuilt pack. Harden loop 2 (2026-10-09), same architecture: round 2's plain solver took the contract-year car as the last link of the chain it was already building and landed 130 kW, so a rung was added after it: the charge, not the settlement record (Curbline's daily 10 a.m. settlement run splits a charge still running into two records that meet end to start; Parking Services' 2026 charging statements reproduce only on the joined charges), from the measured catalogue's #2 (counts file rows instead of the real unit) with #4 behind it. G3 (record versus operation) is listed first among the generators and E stays the architecture's pattern; recorded as the decisive mechanism the new rung reads as D (two grains), which test.same_driver blocks against task115, or as a decisive G3, which ban.pattern blocks against task121, so the clone risk sits on this rung and is reported to the author. Stump, driver, driver_concrete and spine rows restated from the rebuilt pack.
